title: Adaptive quantization CI lint for function-call JSON outputs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add an automated CI lint step that validates function-call / structured JSON outputs produced by FP8/INT8 quantized model variants. The job will run during PR checks and on nightly calibration branches. It combines sampling-based calibration replay, per-field tolerance thresholds (type and semantic tolerances), and an adaptive profile that tightens or relaxes checks based on observed stability metrics. The goal is to catch regressions in schema adherence and critical field fidelity caused by quantization changes before they reach runtime builds.
acceptance_criteria: CI job 'quant-lint-fncall' appears in PR pipelines and passes for mainline models before merging
The lint compares outputs from float32 baseline and target quant profiles (FP8/INT8) using canonicalized JSON and reports field-level deviations with severity tags (break, warn, info)
Adaptive thresholds: job records stability score over last 50 runs and automatically softens non-critical tolerances for noisy fields
Failure modes are triaged into clear actionable summaries and link to a failing-sample artifact and a suggested remapping or calibration tweak
Documentation and runbook for triage added to the quantization-calibration Confluence page
implementation_notes: Prototype will reuse the structured-output canonicalizer from the eval harness but add a lightweight linter that supports: schema path diffing, numeric tolerance windows, enum drift detection, missing/extra key rules, and tokenization-aware string distance heuristics. The CI job should be containerized, accept a baseline model tag and a list of quant profiles, and emit a JSON report to artifacts/GCS. We'll start with a single canonical test harness for the 'payment_dispute.resolve' function-call schema as a representative workload.
test_plan: Create a calibrated sample set (1k seeds) from production prompt corpus scoped to function-call outputs
Run baseline (float32) -> record canonical outputs; run each quant profile and generate diffs
Unit tests for linter rules (missing key, extra key, enum shift, numeric drift with tolerance)
Integrate job into PR pipeline and run against two historical PRs with known regressions to validate detection
Nightly job to compute per-field stability scores and emit dashboard metrics (percent stable, avg drift)
